title: This Is My Family with Sheila Hancock & James Nesbitt - review
transcript: welcome to one minute theater reviews I'm Paul sevel worse this is the Minerva and I'm here to review this is my family this is my family musical by Tim Firth directed by Daniel Evans at Chichester Festival Theatre Minerva there's a lot to like in this is my family Nikki our narrator and the daughter of the family in question sees that her family's falling apart her mum and dad hitting midlife crisis they bicker and they don't seem loving anymore her brothers Moody and withdrawn and her grandmother's beginning to lose her mind Nikki solution is a camping holiday back to where mum and dad first met but like that it sounds quite cliched and predictive organs but Tim Firth has written a beautifully observed drama about families and relationships being young getting old and with some very witty lines some the best of which go to Grandma I played by Sheila Hancock she says that love is when you've sucked off all the chocolate and all you're left with is the nut Oh a mums libido driven sister Shaun played by Rachel Lumbergh this part unlike the others is more of a caricature but it's not the worse for that song comparing lovemaking to driving a car is hilarious and it's a musical play rather than a musical musical mean there are no showstoppers or vocal stretching moments but they're more like words accompanied by music but that may be the point because there are many lovely metaphors in this play that would be too poetic or emotional for spoken dialogue Kirsty McLaren is magnificent as Mickey Scott fallenness lovestruck older brother it's good - and they're antagonistic but loving sibling relationship feels spot-on at the other end of the age scale Sheila Hancock is fabulous as the grandmother who's frightened of what she's losing but finds peace in the past james nesbitt and Claire Bert a pleasure to watch for their comic acting and the set by Richard Kent is super it's the Minerva so push Lisa presided opens but at the back in act one there's a kind of slice through the middle of a house filled with domestic details we send spins around to form a wood in act 2 in the end this is a hopeful view of family life which we can all recognize even if you don't necessarily share it and as I said there's a lot to like in this is my family and I give it four stars if you've enjoyed this review and you want to be the first to know about future reviews please subscribe to my youtube channel 1-minute theater reviews
